title: 黄铜怀表指南针  (The Brass Compass)

segments.t: Two minutes later, Chen steps into Room 9 wiping clean sand from his hands and sets his small brass oil can beside Qing at the sunlit table. Listen first.
老陈，幸亏您来了——我们生怕把彩绘盖子掰弯了。
小晴，老铁盒千万别硬撬；滴一小滴温机油，什么边缘都能松开。
机油要等多久，我们才能试着转边角呀？
数到五，用一根大拇指轻轻按住中间，再平平地往上提。
一、二、三、四、五……啪地一下打开了，一道刮痕都没有！
闻到了吗？雪松木屑、干纸张，还有三十年前淡淡的薄荷香。
哇，老陈，快看最上面绒布小袋子里放着什么！
一个带玻璃盖和蓝钢指针的实心黄铜指南针。
看我把它平放在木桌上，小指针转起来了！
一度都不差——正对着窗外的老梧桐树指向北边。
看黄铜盖子里面：星星旁边刻着几个小小的名字缩写。
制图员出门从不离开好指南针，留下它说明心意很重。
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
老陈，幸亏您来了——我们生怕把彩绘盖子掰弯了。
'Thank goodness you are here, Chen—we were afraid of bending the painted lid.' "Xingkui" is a warm word for "fortunately", and "shengpa" means "for fear of".
小晴，老铁盒千万别硬撬；滴一小滴温机油，什么边缘都能松开。

'Never force old tin, Qing; one tiny drop of warm oil loosens any rim.' "Ying qiao" pairs "by force" with "pry", warning never to force a stuck lid when a drop of "jiyou" (machine oil) will loosen it.
机油要等多久，我们才能试着转边角呀？
'How long does the oil need before we try turning the corners?' "Duojiu" literally asks "how-long-time", and "cai neng" shows that turning the corners happens only after waiting.
数到五，用一根大拇指轻轻按住中间，再平平地往上提。
'Count to five, press the centre gently with one thumb, and lift evenly.' "Damuzhi" literally means "big mother-finger"—the thumb—and doubling "ping" into "pingping" means "flat and evenly".
一、二、三、四、五……啪地一下打开了，一道刮痕都没有！
'One, two, three, four, five... it popped right open without a scratch!' "Pa" imitates the crisp pop of the tin lid releasing, and "yi dao guahen dou meiyou" means "not a single scratch".
闻到了吗？雪松木屑、干纸张，还有三十年前淡淡的薄荷香。
'Smell that? Cedar shavings, dry paper, and faint peppermint from thirty years ago.' "Wen dao" joins "smell" with "catch" for catching a scent, and "bohe xiang" is the cool fragrance of mint.
哇，老陈，快看最上面绒布小袋子里放着什么！
'Oh, Chen, look at what is sitting right on top in a velvet pouch!' "Zui shangmian" means "right on the very top", and "rongbu" combines "velvet" with "cloth" for soft velvet fabric.
一个带玻璃盖和蓝钢指针的实心黄铜指南针。

'A solid brass pocket compass with a glass cover and a blued steel needle.' Mandarin's word for a compass, "zhinanzhen", literally means "south-pointing needle", honoring the ancient south-pointing spoons!
看我把它平放在木桌上，小指针转起来了！
'Watch the little needle spin as I set it flat on the wooden table!' "Zhizhen" pairs "point" and "needle" for a compass needle or clock hand, and "zhuan qilai" means "start spinning".
一度都不差——正对着窗外的老梧桐树指向北边。
'Still balanced to the degree—pointing straight out the window past the shade tree.' "Yi du dou bu cha" means "not off by a single degree", showing how true the brass needle still sits.
看黄铜盖子里面：星星旁边刻着几个小小的名字缩写。
'Look inside the brass cover: there are tiny initials engraved beside a star.' "Ke zhe" means "engraved with", and "suoxie" literally joins "shrink" and "write" for initials.
制图员出门从不离开好指南针，留下它说明心意很重。

'A mapmaker never travels without a good compass, so leaving this behind meant a lot.' "Congbu" is an emphatic "never ever", and "xinyi hen zhong" literally says "the heart's meaning is heavy"—it meant a great deal.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
老陈，幸亏您来了——我们生怕把彩绘盖子掰弯了。

After thirty years underground, the brass pocket compass still points true north past the courtyard tree. See you next time.
明天见！
